title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
capsule: The Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, established 1 August 1953, amalgamated Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia, and Nyasaland into a British-sponsored federal state under Queen Elizabeth II, with Prime Ministers Godfrey Huggins (1953–1956) and Roy Welensky (1956–1963) presiding over a government in which political power was reserved for the white settler minority. Designed to pool the copper-belt revenues of Northern Rhodesia with Southern Rhodesia's agricultural and industrial base, the federation achieved economic growth while systematically excluding the African majority from meaningful representation. African nationalist movements across all three territories, the 1959 Nyasaland Emergency, and the Macmillan government's decolonization policy led the Monckton Commission (1960) to recommend dissolution; the federation was formally wound up on 31 December 1963, with Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland becoming independent as Zambia and Malawi in 1964.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial boundaries are precisely defined by British colonial legislation and are well documented; internal administrative divisions between the three component territories are clearly delineated in the 1953 Federal Constitution.
